name: Tool-using agent
description: The local model decides whether a tool is needed. When it is, the tool runs (auto-selected from the registry) and a summariser folds the result into the final answer; when it is not, the model's own answer goes straight to the reply. Good template for action-oriented tasks.

samplePrompts.title: Look up the population of Chile
When was the Eiffel Tower opened?

config.systemPrompt:
You decide how to answer the user. Today is $DATE. Available tools:
$TOOLS

If a tool can produce more reliable or fresher information than your own knowledge, output ONLY the search term or the short description of what the tool should do — no preamble, no explanation, nothing else. Otherwise answer the user's question directly and completely, in at most two short paragraphs.

The next step decides which of the two you produced, so do not mix them: either a lookup request on its own, or a finished answer on its own. Never output an empty response — when the input is empty or meaningless, say so in one sentence as a finished answer.

Reply in the user's language ($LANG).

config.conditionPrompt:
The upstream text is a request for a lookup rather than a finished answer — the previous step decided that a tool is needed. Answer true when the text is a search term, a topic name, or a short description of what to look up. Answer false when the text already answers the user's original question on its own, including when it says the request cannot be answered.

Output exactly one word — true or false — in lowercase, with no punctuation, quotation marks or explanation.
